newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Focus-S-E-Banken says Q1 up on lower loan losses.
newsitem.headline: Focus-S-E-Banken says Q1 up on lower loan losses.

text.p: Falling loan losses and a boost in net interest income lifted Swedish bank S-E-Banken's first quarter operating profit 17 percent to 1.50 billion crowns ($192.2 million), the bank said on Tuesday.
The profit was higher than expected with analysts targeting 1.38 billion crowns in a Reuter poll.

But the report got a lukewarm reception on the Stockholm Stock Exchange where the bank's share was flat at 80.50 crowns at 1150 GMT after having traded in a tight range between 80.5 and 81 crowns both before and after the report.
Meanwhile, the bourse's general index was up 0.51 percent at 2,591.05.

S-E-Banken's loan losses dropped 62 percent to 165 million crowns, including value changes in assets taken over and the withdrawal of a 95 million crown country risk provision concerning Peru, the bank said in its earnings statement.
The lending loss level fell to 0.24 percent from 0.69 percent, while doubtful claims dropped 19 percent to 4.96 billion crowns.

Net interest income jumped 46 percent to 2.24 billion crowns, mainly as a result of a larger gap between longterm and shortterm interest rates in the first quarter than in the corresponding three month period a year earlier, the bank said.
Net commission rose 18 percent to 1.31 billion crowns, largely fuelled by increased volumes within equities trading where the bank's market share rose to 12.3 percent from 11.2.
Deposits and lending also improved, up eight percent to 153 billion crowns and up 10 percent to 266 billion crowns, respectively.
"This means that the bank's (deposit) market share increased from 17.0 percent to 18.4 percent," the bank said.
Net financial transactions dropped 68 percent to 332 million crowns, mainly as rising interest rates at the end of the period had a negative impact on the bank's liquidity and trading portfolios.
Total costs also rose, up 13 percent to 2.34 billion crowns, partly because of Nordic expansion and continued investment in advisory services and computer systems.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.804 Swedish Crowns)
